hero.headline: Your data is being harvested. Here's how to take it back.
hero.subhead: Every app you use, every search you make, every message you send — someone's collecting it. This is your pocket guide to swapping the tools that spy on you for ones that don't.

questions.heading: What is digital privacy?
points: It's not about having something to hide — it's about controlling who gets to see your stuff
It's the right to exist online without being tracked, profiled, and sold
Think of it like curtains on your windows: you're not doing anything wrong, you just don't want strangers watching

questions.heading: Why should you care?
points: Your data can be used to manipulate what you see, buy, and believe
Once it's out there, you can't get it back — data breaches are forever
Companies make billions selling your attention. You see $0 of that
Privacy isn't about going off-grid. It's about choosing what you share and with whom

intro.encryption_blurb: **Encryption** scrambles your data so only you and the person you're talking to can read it. Without it, your messages, emails, and files are basically postcards — anyone handling them along the way can read what's inside. End-to-end encryption (E2EE) means not even the company providing the service can see your content. It's the difference between a sealed letter and a postcard.

categories.label: Browsing & Search
categories.tagline: Stop letting your browser rat you out.

groups.label: Browsers

tools.name: Brave
tools.note: Blocks ads & trackers by default. Looks like Chrome, acts nothing like it.

tools.name: Firefox
tools.note: Independent, non-profit, customizable. Add uBlock Origin and you're golden.

tools.name: LibreWolf
tools.note: Firefox with all telemetry ripped out. Hardened privacy, zero phone-home.

tools.name: Mullvad Browser
tools.note: Tor-level fingerprint protection without the Tor speed hit. Built with the Tor Project.

groups.quick_win: Install uBlock Origin on whatever browser you use. It's free, open-source, and kills 90% of tracking. Takes 10 seconds.

tools.name: DuckDuckGo
tools.note: No tracking, no profiling, no filter bubble. Same search, no spyware.

tools.name: Brave Search
tools.note: Independent index (not Bing/Google reskinned). Anonymous results.

tools.name: SearxNG
tools.note: Self-hostable meta-search. Queries multiple engines, strips trackers.

groups.label: VPN

tools.name: ProtonVPN
tools.note: Swiss-based, open-source, audited. Free tier exists and doesn't suck.

tools.name: Mullvad
tools.note: No account, no email, pay with cash. The most anonymous VPN setup possible.

tools.name: IVPN
tools.note: Independently audited, no-log policy, WireGuard support.

replaces: Free VPNs that sell your data
groups.use_case: Use on public Wi-Fi, to bypass blocks, and to stop your ISP from selling your browsing history.
groups.quick_win: Even a free VPN is better than no VPN on airport/cafe Wi-Fi. But paid ones don't sell your data.

categories.label: Messaging & Mail
categories.tagline: Your conversations shouldn't be someone's business model.

groups.label: Messaging

tools.name: Signal
tools.note: Gold standard for encrypted chat. Non-profit, open-source, audited. Just use it.

tools.name: SimpleX Chat
tools.note: Zero identifiers. No phone number, no email, no user ID. Audited by Trail of Bits. For when you need to go dark.

tools.name: BitChat
tools.note: Bluetooth mesh messaging. Works with zero internet. For protests, festivals, or when the grid goes down.

groups.quick_win: Getting your friends on Signal is the single highest-impact privacy swap you can make. It's free, easy, and works exactly like WhatsApp.

tools.name: Proton Mail
tools.note: Encrypted inbox, zero-access architecture. Even Proton can't read your mail.

tools.name: Tuta Mail
tools.note: German-made, fully open-source, E2EE calendar included.

groups.label: Socials

tools.name: Nostr — Primal
tools.note: Nostr social client. Your followers belong to you, not the platform.

tools.name: Nostr — Amethyst
tools.note: Open-source Nostr client for Android.

tools.name: Nostr — YakiHonne
tools.note: Nostr-based content platform. Own your social graph, be uncensorable.

groups.use_case: Nostr is a protocol, not a platform. Your account isn't owned by any company. Switch clients whenever you want — your followers come with you.

tools.name: Jitsi Meet
tools.note: Open-source, no account needed. Just share a link and you're in.

tools.name: Proton Meet
tools.note: E2EE video calls from the Proton ecosystem.

categories.label: Collaboration & Files
categories.tagline: Your documents shouldn't live on someone else's server.

groups.label: Cloud & Docs

tools.name: Proton Drive
tools.note: Encrypted cloud storage + file sharing. Swiss, audited, generous free tier.

tools.name: Proton Docs
tools.note: Real-time collaborative docs — encrypted end-to-end.

tools.name: Proton Sheets
tools.note: Encrypted spreadsheets. Your formulas, nobody else's business.

tools.name: CryptPad
tools.note: Full encrypted office suite — docs, slides, forms, whiteboards.

tools.name: Nextcloud
tools.note: Self-hosted Google Workspace replacement. Files, calendar, tasks, video calls — all yours.

groups.quick_win: Moving your most sensitive docs to Proton Drive is free and instant. Full migration can wait.

tools.name: Element
tools.note: Matrix-based, federated, self-hostable. Like Discord but you own the server.

tools.name: Buzz
tools.note: Self-hostable team chat with AI agents built in.

tools.name: AnyType
tools.note: Local-first workspace. Your data lives on your device, encrypted.

tools.name: Standard Notes
tools.note: Zero-knowledge note-taking. Even they can't read your notes.

tools.name: Formstr
tools.note: Nostr-based forms. Collect responses without feeding a data monster.

groups.label: Photos

tools.name: Immich
tools.note: Self-hosted Google Photos replacement. One of the fastest-growing open-source projects right now.

tools.name: Ente Photos
tools.note: E2EE photo backup that's hosted for you. No self-hosting required.

groups.quick_win: Immich + an old laptop or NAS = your own private Google Photos. Tutorials are everywhere on YouTube.

tools.name: Rumble
tools.note: Fewer restrictions, less algorithm curation.

categories.label: AI
categories.tagline: Ask AI without handing over your entire digital life.

groups.label: Private AI Chat

tools.name: Proton Lumo
tools.note: Encrypted AI chat. Your conversations aren't training data.

tools.name: Venice
tools.note: Private, decentralized AI. No account, no tracking.

tools.name: Brave Leo
tools.note: AI built into Brave. No sign-up, no data retention.

tools.name: Maple
tools.note: Privacy-first AI assistant.

groups.quick_win: If you're asking AI about medical, legal, or personal stuff, use a privacy-respecting option. Your prompts shouldn't be anyone's dataset.

groups.label: Local AI (Runs on Your Device)

tools.name: Ollama
tools.note: Run LLMs on your laptop. Data never leaves your machine. It's actually that simple.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.note: One API, hundreds of models. Route queries to whichever AI you want.

tools.name: Goose
tools.note: Local AI agent framework. Automate tasks without leaking data.

tools.name: Odysseus
tools.note: Local AI built for sensitive data queries.

groups.use_case: Anything sensitive — financial docs, health questions, work emails — should go through local AI, not a cloud service that logs everything.

tools.name: MacParakeet
tools.note: On-device transcription for macOS. Audio never touches a server.

categories.label: Operating Systems
categories.tagline: The deepest layer of control. Start here if you're serious.

groups.label: Desktop

tools.name: Ubuntu
tools.note: Most beginner-friendly Linux. Huge community, works out of the box.

tools.name: Linux Mint
tools.note: Looks like Windows, acts like Linux. Smoothest transition for switchers.

tools.name: Tails
tools.note: Boot from USB, leave no trace on the computer. The Edward Snowden OS.

groups.quick_win: You don't have to switch your main OS. Try Linux on a USB stick first — Tails or Ubuntu Live. Zero commitment.

tools.name: GrapheneOS
tools.note: Hardened Android. Strips Google out completely. For Pixel phones.

tools.name: CalyxOS
tools.note: Privacy-focused Android with optional micro-services. Gentler than Graphene.

categories.label: Passwords & 2FA
categories.tagline: Use a different password everywhere. Without remembering any of them.

groups.label: Password Managers

tools.name: Bitwarden
tools.note: Open-source, free tier covers everything. 40M+ users. Set it up once, never think about passwords again.

tools.name: Proton Pass
tools.note: Encrypted vault + email aliases. Stop giving your real email to every site.

groups.quick_win: This is the #1 thing to do. Right now. Stop reading and go set up Bitwarden. It's free.

tools.name: Proton Authenticator
tools.note: Encrypted 2FA with cloud sync. Lose your phone? Still get your codes.

tools.name: Ente Authenticator
tools.note: Open-source 2FA with encrypted backup. Self-hostable.

categories.label: Maps
categories.tagline: Get directions without broadcasting where you're going.

groups.label: Navigation

tools.name: OrganicMaps
tools.note: Offline-first, no tracking. Download your city, navigate without signal or surveillance.

tools.name: OsmAnd
tools.note: Power-user maps. Hiking trails, cycling routes, the works.

groups.quick_win: OrganicMaps looks and feels like Google Maps. Your grandparents wouldn't notice the switch.

categories.label: Money & Payments
categories.tagline: Financial tools that don't ask for your life story.

groups.label: Virtual Cards

tools.name: 2Fiat
tools.note: Virtual debit cards. Spend online without exposing your real card.

replaces: Using your real card on every website

tools.name: FixedFloat
tools.note: P2P non-KYC exchange. No passport required.

tools.name: uBlock Origin
tools.note: Not just an ad blocker — a tracking exterminator. Install on every browser.

tools.name: VeraCrypt
tools.note: Encrypt files, partitions, or entire drives. Military-grade, open-source.

tools.name: Excalidraw
tools.note: Open-source whiteboarding. Draw diagrams without an account.

tools.name: SilentLink
tools.note: Anonymous e-SIMs. Borderless mobile internet, no ID required.

tools.name: SMS4Sats
tools.note: Send/receive SMS privately.

tools.name: Citadel Chat
tools.note: Offline, off-grid knowledge base & AI. For when you want zero connection.

reading_list.title: The Machinery of Freedom
